work.title: Rain in Summer
work.note: Rain in Summer é um poema do americano Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, publicado em 1845. A referência abre a situação para praticar “dizer o que o tempo está fazendo agora: It’s raining (está chovendo) e It’s pouring (chove forte)”.

facts.label: Contar o fim de semana
facts.sub: Pergunte com How was…? e did + verbo base (What did you cook?). Responda no passado: I stayed home, I watched a movie, we went to the beach.

facts.label: Conversa de segunda
facts.sub: Nos escritórios dos EUA, a segunda começa com perguntas leves sobre o fim de semana. A conversa é curta e positiva, e ajuda a criar laço com a equipe.

facts.label: Planos do fim de semana
facts.sub: As respostas mais comuns falam de filmes, passeios, comida e família. Dizer “I stayed home” é normal, e ninguém espera um grande evento.

compare.br: In Brazil, people also ask about the fim de semana, often with more detail and plans for the next one.
compare.us: In the USA, small talk is short and light. Answers use the simple past: I stayed home, we went to the beach.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “How was your weekend?” is a common Monday question.
items.why: It is a friendly way to start the week.

items.s: You must answer with a long story.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

pages.title: Coffee on Monday · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning at a busy office in Chicago. People walk in with coffee and tired faces. Evan stops next to the coffee machine and smiles. “**Good morning! How was your weekend?**” he asks.
“**It was great. How about yours?**” says Rosa. “**Pretty quiet. I stayed home,**” says Evan. “**Did you do anything fun?**” she asks. “I watched a movie and cooked,” he says.

pages.focus: final -ed em stayed, cooked e watched
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: O -ed final tem três sons: /d/ em stayed, /t/ em watched e cooked (/kukt/) e /id/ em wanted. Muitos brasileiros acrescentam um “i”.
pages.how: Em stayed termine com um D leve, sem vogal. Em cooked e watched, termine com T leve. Não diga “stêidi” nem “cúkedi”.
pages.tip: Fale a palavra e feche a boca no final: o T ou D deve ser quase um clique.
